clusters.state_of_play: Russia's escalating drone campaign includes jet-powered drones striking Kyiv and a strike on the Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train near the Polish border, which experts now suspect was an intended target rather than incidental, minutes after it carried foreign dignitaries including Boris Johnson, Carl Bildt, and reportedly ex-CIA director David Petraeus from a Kyiv security summit. Poland scrambled fighter jets amid the overnight barrage of 450+ drones and missiles that killed six and injured over 40 nationwide, and jointly with Ukraine condemned the strike as an 'escalation.' NATO separately shot down a Russian drone over Lithuania, though the drone's origin is now disputed, with some reports citing Belarus and others saying it is unknown. Security incidents have also intensified elsewhere in Europe, including Denmark, prompting EU allies to discuss strengthening NATO's eastern flank. NATO chief Mark Rutte has pledged increased Ukraine support, framing the border strikes as a sign of Russian desperation and vowing the alliance will not be intimidated, while former UK defence secretary Ben Wallace has urged Britain to shoot down Russian drones threatening Nato territory. Ukraine continues drone strikes on Russian refineries and oil tankers, prompting President Trump to publicly urge Kyiv to halt attacks on Russian oil infrastructure amid surging global diesel prices, while Jared Kushner's proposal for Ukraine to cede Russian-demanded territory draws criticism at a diplomatic forum. Fighting persists near the Polish border, including a fresh strike on the town of Yahodyn just 2km from Poland.

Zelenskyy's plane was reportedly nearly struck by a drone shortly after departing Moldova for the funeral; Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Store confirmed the incident, an official traveling with Zelenskyy believes a Russian weapon was involved, while a Ukrainian source suggested the threat may have been overstated. Meanwhile, William made a surprise public appearance with Catherine at Everton's stadium to launch a new suicide prevention campaign, an 'On Your Side' toolkit developed with figures including Harry Kane, George Russell, Alan Shearer and broadcaster Gabby Logan, marking his first royal outing since the summer break amid the ongoing Harry and Meghan letter row.
